newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine labor law progress to be slow -minister.
newsitem.headline: Argentine labor law progress to be slow -minister.

text.p: The Argentine government's program of changing labor laws to cut costs is likely to be passed slowly due to October's Congressional elections, Labor Minister Armando Caro Figueroa said in an interview Sunday.
Caro Figueroa told newspaper La Nacion that the government wanted to push laws to cut labor costs through Congress, and was unlikely to try and repeat its attempt last year to pass them by decree.

"This is a pre-electoral stage in which whether the social and political alliance in the country is maintained or is broken is at stake," Caro Figueroa said, "If you ask me whether we have to delay the reform to consolidate the political alliance, then I say 'Let's delay the issue of dismissals and collective bargaining.'
"The priority is to consolidate the alliance and then win the elections," he said.
Unions held a general strike after the government tried to pass a range of measures to cut employers' costs by decree late last year. The decrees were later overturned by the courts.
Government-sponsored talks between unions and business to agree on new labor rules have so far failed to make much progress.
